commenter_information.stakeholder_type: Professional Association / Technology Vendor Association / Provider Association
commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: National organization representing health IT companies serving LTPAC providers, rehabilitation therapy companies, and providers of mobile clinical laboratory and portable x-ray services for SNFs, senior living, and homebound patients; founding member of Long Term & Post-Acute Care Health IT Collaborative.

executive_summary: ADVION responds to the laboratory RFI by warning that prior authorization is poorly suited to mobile clinical laboratory services in long-term and post-acute care, where same-day testing guides immediate clinical decisions. It urges CMS not to impose PA for LTPAC clinical labs, or if CMS proceeds, to use exemptions, phased implementation, technical assistance, real-time decisions, documentation alignment, and standards-based workflows reflecting the sector’s limited health IT infrastructure.

detailed_positions.topic: Prior authorization for mobile clinical labs in LTPAC
detailed_positions.rationale: Mobile labs collect/process specimens same day for medically fragile SNF/homebound patients; PA delays would disrupt time-sensitive diagnosis and treatment decisions.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Do not impose prior authorization for clinical laboratory services in the long-term and post-acute care sector.

detailed_positions.rationale: SNFs, ancillary providers, and mobile labs often lack full EHR interoperability, API readiness, and integrated PA workflows because they did not receive HITECH-era support.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Account for LTPAC, home health, rural, and resource-constrained settings through phased implementation, technical assistance, and realistic timelines.

detailed_positions.rationale: Ordering clinicians may not be present during collection, systems may not flag PA, and specimens cannot be held without risking integrity.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Avoid PA processes that assume a pre-service window; preserve same-day testing workflows and avoid requirements that make labs wait for PA before processing.

detailed_positions.rationale: Electronic exchange can reduce manual work if aligned with existing workflows and minimum necessary documentation.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Promote standardized ePA workflows, structured data elements, standard terminology, cloud-enabled solutions, and interoperable APIs while avoiding proprietary portals and custom interfaces.

detailed_positions.topic: Exemptions, real-time decisions, and documentation alignment
detailed_positions.rationale: PA may be inappropriate for high-volume, routine, low-risk services and should not delay care where necessary.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Exempt certain settings/patient types/items when clinical criteria are met; if PA remains, require real-time or near-real-time decisions, clear appeals, and common documentation standards.

solicitation_responses.summary: Responds to the laboratory tests/DMEPOS RFI, focusing on mobile labs serving SNFs and homebound/LTPAC patients, workflow infeasibility, IT readiness gaps, and need for exemptions or phased approaches.
Addresses implementation feasibility, timeline, resource constraints, small/resource-limited provider impacts, and technical readiness in LTPAC settings.

recommendations: Do not impose prior authorization for clinical laboratory services in long-term and post-acute care.
Exempt certain settings, patient types, high-volume routine tests, or low-risk items when clinical criteria are met.
If PA remains, support real-time or near-real-time decisions and clear appeals pathways.
Account for LTPAC, home health, rural, and resource-constrained operational realities.
Provide phased implementation, technical assistance, and clear timelines.
Encourage common documentation standards for lab tests.
Promote cloud-enabled and standards-based workflows that reduce proprietary portals and custom interfaces.
Use structured data, standard terminology, and interoperable APIs to exchange minimum necessary clinical documentation directly from EHRs.

primary_concerns: PA is unworkable for same-day mobile lab services.
Specimen integrity and patient care may suffer if testing waits for authorization.
LTPAC settings lack the health IT infrastructure assumed by FHIR/API workflows.
potential_negative_impacts_cited: Worse outcomes, avoidable hospitalizations, higher system costs, delayed treatment changes, medication delays, inability to act on critical results, administrative burden on labs and SNFs.
implementation_barriers_mentioned: Legacy systems, limited IT staffing, lack of EHR/lab integration, no point-of-order PA mechanism, ordering clinician not physically present, difficulty obtaining documentation, specimen degradation.

data_or_statistics_cited: CDC estimate that roughly 70 percent of healthcare decisions depend on laboratory test results.
Results are typically reported by early afternoon/same day in mobile lab workflows.
studies_or_research_referenced: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention statement on lab testing role in healthcare decisions.
examples_provided: Mobile laboratory technicians travel to LTC facilities, collect specimens bedside, transport them, process them, and report same-day results.
Critical results guide decisions to hospitalize patients or change medications.

impact_assessment.economic_implications: PA delays could increase avoidable hospitalizations and system costs; implementation could impose costs on under-resourced LTPAC providers and ancillary vendors.
impact_assessment.technical_feasibility: Current LTPAC infrastructure is often not ready for rapid FHIR/API PA mandates; standards-based workflows may be feasible only with assistance and phased timelines.
impact_assessment.patient_care_impact: High; timely lab results directly guide diagnosis, medication changes, treatment initiation, and hospitalization decisions for medically fragile patients.

sentiment_analysis.overall_position: Opposed to PA for LTPAC clinical labs; supportive of careful interoperability modernization

key_quotes: Results are often provided same day which makes this service highly inappropriate and unworkable for prior authorization.

Delays in this context do not simply create administrative inconvenience; they translate directly into worse outcomes for the patient, avoidable hospitalizations, and significantly higher costs to the system.

Prior authorization requirements that assume a pre-service window for PA submission simply do not reflect the realities of how laboratory medicine, and particularly mobile laboratory medicine in post-acute and long-term care settings, works.
Prior authorization processes are not a one size fits all.
